newsitem.title: THAILAND: Dozens of Vietnamese boat people stab themselves.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of Vietnamese boat people stab themselves.

text.p: Dozens of Vietnamese boat people stranded in Thailand stabbed themselves to avoid forced repatriation on Thursday and 17 were taken to hospital, police and hospital officials said.

Some 57 Vietnamese asylum seekers who have been living in the Sikhiu holding camp in Nakhon Ratchasima, about 250 km (150 miles) northeast of Bangkok, cut themselves on Wednesday after they learned they were to be repatriated to Vietnam on Thursday, the officials said.
"Seventeen of them were hospitalised and four women are still in serious condition," a hospital official told Reuters.
Despite the violent protest authorities were able to send back some 200 refugees on Thursday morning including those who had cut themselves but were not hospitalised, police said.

Nearly 2,000 Vietnamese who were denied settlement in a third country and were stranded in the Sikhiu holding camp are due to be sent back to Vietnam by the end of September under the Orderly Departure Programme.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) ceased all funding for Vietnamese asylum seekers in Thailand and other countries in the region in June.
The UNHCR, the Southeast Asian "first asylum" countries and Vietnam agreed at a meeting in Bangkok in January that the 20,000 asylum seekers in camps in the region would be sent home.

The Vietnamese at the Sikhiu camp have all been interviewed by UNHCR officials and judged to be economic migrants rather than genuine refugees. As such, they were subject to Thai immigration laws, the UNHCR officials said.
More than 500 Vietnamese have been sent home from Thailand since the programme started in late June.

Virtually all the Vietnamese asylum seekers in the region fled their country in flimsy boats after the 1975 communist victory. About a quarter of those in Thailand arrived by land after travelling through Cambodia.
